Our training objective, RealmMatch, constructs a likelihood score matrix across image--response combinations and combines supervised learning with bidirectional contrastive losses to reinforce correct matches and suppress mismatches. Compared with the original Qwen3.5-9B model, DreamRealm improves performance across six visual perception and hallucination benchmarks, including gains of 7.26 percentage points in HallusionBench accuracy and 11.34 percentage points in MMVP pair accuracy. Together with ablation studies on data construction and training methods, these results demonstrate that hallucination assignment is a promising paradigm for improving visual perception and mitigating hallucinations.

items.title_en: TOP: Transmission-Oriented Remote Sensing Pansharpening
items.abstract_en: Pansharpening has been extensively studied as a fundamental image fusion task in remote sensing. However, most existing methods focus on improving fusion quality under the implicit assumption that high-resolution observations have already been fully downlinked to the ground. As a result, existing models are highly vulnerable to perturbations introduced by lossy compression used for downlink transmission. To address this limitation, we present, to the best of our knowledge, the first transmission oriented pansharpening (TOP) framework, which unifies compact latent coding, onboard pansharpening, and efficient downlink transmission within a single satellite-toground pipeline. TOP encodes remote-sensing observations into a compact binary latent space, where a lightweight onboard fusion module can efficiently predict the fused binary latent code. Since only the compact fused code is downlinked, the transmission payload is substantially reduced. Overall, TOP enables low-payload downlink and lightweight onboard processing while maintaining high fusion quality under severe bandwidth constraints. Experiments across multispectral and hyperspectral settings show that TOP consistently achieves superior fusion quality at higher compression ratios than representative pansharpening methods paired with standard lossy codecs. For example, on GaoFen-2, TOP attains a fusion PSNR of 31.4 dB at a downlink compression ratio of 50x. This design also points toward transmissionoriented processing for other remote-sensing tasks. The code will be made available at https://github.com/JingZe-Liang/TOP.git.

items.title_en: Unaligned Image Guided Denoising via Cross-modal Conditional Flow Matching
items.abstract_en: This work presents UGD-FM, a novel unaligned image guided denoising framework based on cross-modal conditional flow matching. Unlike previous approaches that assume spatially aligned inputs or only handle small-baseline rectified pairs, we address a more challenging setting where severe target noise and large-range two-dimensional cross-modal misalignment coexist. Specifically, we formulate guided denoising as a progressive flow matching process, allowing image restoration and aligned guidance aggregation to mutually reinforce each other. To support efficient few-step inference, we introduce a stage-focused and inference-consistent training strategy that focuses on task-critical denoising stages, and mitigates the training-inference mismatch. We further propose adaptive sparse guidance propagation for efficient and reliable large-range matching, regularized by perceptual and geometric auxiliary losses. Experiments demonstrate that UGD-FM achieves state-of-the-art denoising performance with only one or two inference steps, and is compatible with modern single-image restoration backbones.

items.title_en: Entropogram-guided Visual Realignment Decoding: Capturing the Rhythm of Multimodal Reasoning
items.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress on cross-modal reasoning tasks, yet they continue to suffer from hallucinations in long-chain reasoning processes. In this work, we revisit hallucination in MLLMs from the perspective of reasoning generation dynamics. We argue that entropy is not merely a static measure of uncertainty but a structured signal that reflects how modality information is integrated throughout decoding. Through systematic analysis, we identify two characteristic entropy patterns associated with hallucination behaviors: (1) a generally high-confidence regime corresponds to premature convergence to inappropriate multimodal interactions; and (2) local abrupt entropy transitions are associated with reasoning instability and hallucination onset. Building on these observations, we propose an entropy-aware self-introspective framework for MLLM reasoning. Our method continuously tracks entropy dynamics during decoding and performs targeted visual re-alignment when suspicious hallucination states are detected, encouraging the model to re-examine salient visual evidence at critical reasoning stages. Extensive experiments across six multimodal reasoning benchmarks spanning nine distinct evaluation settings demonstrate that our approach delivers robust improvements in reasoning accuracy and hallucination robustness, while providing new insights into the generation dynamics underlying MLLM failures. The code is available at: https://github.com/jden4524/SelfRetrospectiveDecoding.

items.title_en: A Bag of Tricks for Defending Deep Learning-based Face Recognition Pipelines against Backdoor Attacks
items.abstract_en: The protection of mature, multi-stage Face Recognition Systems is crucial to system providers. This technical report targets the threat model most relevant to industry practitioners: although model training is performed in-house, training data is sourced from possibly-compromised third parties. Given this setting, we present three practical defense "tricks" against data poisoning-based backdoor attacks. The first operates at training-time, detecting poisoned identities during training or prior to a pipeline's deployment. The last two operate at inference-time, filtering suspicious inputs before an answer can be sent back to a potential attacker. Each method is presented with their motivation, algorithms and computational impact, and evaluated on realistic face recognition workloads. Our goal is to provide actionable hardening techniques to system providers.

items.title_en: Ventilation Perfusion Functional Difference Images in Lung SPECT: a linear and symmetrical scale as an alternative to the Ventilation Perfusion Ratio
items.abstract_en: Purpose: Ventilation Perfusion SPECT is important in the diagnostics of e.g. pulmonary embolism and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Classical and reverse mismatched defects can be identified by utilizing the ventilation-perfusion ratio. Unfortunately, this ratio is only linear in the ventilation, the scale is not symmetrical regarding classical and reversed mismatches and small perfusion values give rise to artifacts. The ventilation-perfusion (VQ) difference is developed as an alternative. Methods: For both VQ-ratio and VQ-difference a scaling factor for the perfusion is computed, so that voxels with matched ventilation and perfusion (on average) yield zero signal. The relative VQ-difference is calculated by scaling with the summed VQ-signal in each voxel. The scaled VQ-difference is calculated by scaling with the global maximum of this sum. Results: The relative and scaled differences have a scale from -1 (perfusion only) to +1 (ventilation only). Image quality of relative VQ-difference and VQ-ratio images is hampered by artifacts from areas with both low perfusion and low ventilation. Ratio and differences have been investigated in ten patients and are shown for three patients (one without defects). Clinical thresholds for the difference images are derived resulting in color maps of relevant (reversed) mismatches with a (reciprocal) ratio larger than two. Conclusions: The relative ventilation-perfusion difference is a methodological improvement on the ventilation-perfusion ratio, because it has a symmetrical scale and is bound on a closed domain. A better diagnostic value is expected by utilizing the scaled difference, which represents functional difference instead of relative difference.

items.title_en: UniLoop: Unified Loop Closure Detection from Retrieval to Geometric Verification and Relative Pose Estimation
items.abstract_en: Loop closure detection conventionally cascades separate models for global retrieval, geometric verification, and relative pose estimation, leading to redundant computation and disconnected visual representations. We propose UniLoop, a unified framework that reuses the hierarchical representations of the pretrained geometric foundation model throughout this pipeline. A shared image encoder produces features for compact global descriptors; the same features are passed to the cross-view decoder for pairwise verification; and the original geometric predictions provide relative camera constraints for pose-graph optimization. Experiments on place recognition, loop verification, and relative pose estimation show that UniLoop improves loop-closure robustness and accuracy while reducing redundant backbone computation relative to modular pipelines. UniLoop achieves the best Recall@10 on MSLS (96.6) and Pitts30k (99.3) among the compared methods, while its verification branch reaches 95.63 AP and 96.29 ROC-AUC, surpassing the existing geometric verification baselines.

items.title_en: NanoKV: High-Ratio KV Cache Compression for Autoregressive Video Generation
items.abstract_en: Autoregressive video models rely on historical key-value (KV) caches to preserve scene consistency over extended rollouts, making KV storage and repeated attention over history a growing memory and computational bottleneck. Aggressive compression can degrade generation quality, while reconstructing full-dimensional KV leaves attention computation largely unchanged. We introduce NanoKV, a frozen-backbone framework for generation-aware high-ratio KV compression. NanoKV exploits redundancy across tokens and attention heads by storing shared content in cluster centers and encoding joint head-channel residuals into low-bit coefficients. Crucially, NanoKV uses different fitting objectives for Keys and Values according to their distinct roles in attention: Key decoders are optimized to preserve downstream block outputs, whereas Value encoders and decoders are fitted for faithful reconstruction through the deployed quantization path. Building on the same compressed representation, the optional NanoKV-Fast variant reuses the stored coefficients for mixed-dimensional attention, reducing computation without modifying the video backbone. Across three autoregressive video backbones, NanoKV consistently improves the quality-storage trade-off. On HY-WorldPlay, NanoKV achieves $26.09\times$ effective KV compression, nearly twice that of KVTC, while improving PSNR by 1.0 dB. NanoKV-Fast retains $20.53\times$ effective compression and achieves an approximately $1.15\times$ end-to-end speedup over KVTC.

items.title_en: FlashRelight: Portrait Video Relighting with Dynamic Lighting
items.abstract_en: Portrait video relighting aims to modify the illumination of a portrait video while preserving photorealism and temporal stability. The task becomes particularly challenging under dynamic lighting, where illumination direction, intensity, and color vary over time. To tackle this problem, we introduce FlashRelight, a novel two-stage framework for dynamic portrait video relighting. FlashRelight first suppresses the source illumination through delighting, and then synthesizes the target dynamic lighting on an illumination-neutral portrait video. FlashRelight supports three complementary control modalities: envmap sequences for explicit frame-level lighting control, dynamic lighting text for semantic illumination editing, and lighting reference videos for visual lighting transfer. Training follows a low-cost hybrid strategy that combines static one-light-at-a-time (OLAT) data with generated dynamic-lighting portrait videos, covering both controlled illumination variation and realistic portrait motion. Extensive experiments show that FlashRelight achieves temporally coherent and photorealistic dynamic relighting while enabling flexible cross-video lighting transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/vivoCameraResearch/FlashRelight

items.title_en: Traffic-VL: Reinforced Vision-Language Models for Generalizable End-to-End Traffic Signal Control
items.abstract_en: Existing traffic signal control methods typically rely on structured traffic states produced by dedicated perception pipelines. Emerging visual approaches often use idealized simulator images and convert them into intermediate representations before control, limiting their ability to directly exploit roadside visual observations. To bridge both the visual-domain and perception-to-decision gaps, we introduce SynTra-V and Traffic-VL. SynTra-V converts physics-based traffic simulations into photorealistic multi-view surveillance imagery across diverse road topologies and sensing conditions, and automatic semantic auditing checks that control-critical geometry, vehicle movements, and lane semantics match the simulator state. Traffic-VL is an eight-billion-parameter vision-language model that directly maps synchronized multi-view images and natural-language phase descriptions to signal decisions without intermediate structured states. Building on Traffic-R1's two-stage reinforced reasoning framework, Traffic-VL adapts its vision encoder via offline reinforcement learning on SynTra-V and freezes it during online visual stepwise trajectory policy optimization in closed-loop simulation. Experiments show that Traffic-VL matches structured-state Traffic-R1 while outperforming image-based controllers and general-purpose vision-language models, including Gemini 3 Pro. Evaluations on unseen topologies, degraded sensing conditions, real surveillance footage, and a three-week deployment across ten intersections further demonstrate robust visual generalization and effective constrained online control.

items.title_en: Prism: Bidirectional Self-Teaching for Unified Multimodal Models
items.abstract_en: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single model. Existing post-training methods either use understanding as a fixed teacher to improve generation, or rely on ground-truth trajectories to supervise both understanding and generation. Prism instead derives bidirectional supervision from self-generated interleaved rollouts, constructing training targets according to the reliability of their text and image chains. We propose Prism, a bidirectional self-teaching post-training method for UMMs. Like a prism decomposing mixed light, Prism decouples a coupled interleaved trajectory into a text chain and an image chain, assesses the reliability of each chain, and constructs a corresponding training target from their reliability states. Experiments on both SenseNova-U1 and BAGEL show that Prism improves both understanding and generation. On the generation side, GenEval improves from 85.8 to 89.2 (+3.4), and DPG improves from 86.1 to 87.3 (+1.2) on SenseNova-U1. On the understanding side, the total MME score improves from 2282.6 to 2311.6, and MMVP improves from 58.0 to 62.0. Consistent improvements are observed on BAGEL. These results highlight that Prism enables coordinated improvements in generation and understanding by constructing reliability-guided self-training targets from self-generated trajectories, without relying on an external verifier or externally annotated corrected trajectories during target construction.

items.title_en: Beyond Scene Shortcuts: Action-Centric Video-Text Alignment for Fine-Grained Action Understanding
items.abstract_en: Fine-grained action understanding requires vision-language models to ground what an agent does, how it acts, and why it acts in spatio-temporal evidence. However, richer supervision can backfire: fine-tuned models may generate detailed action descriptions grounded in static scenes and salient objects rather than motion, a failure we call Environment-Grounded Action Hallucination (EGAH). To mitigate EGAH, we propose Staged Attention Rectification and Reinforcement (STARR), an action-centric video-text alignment framework that breaks scene-action shortcuts through Action-Environment Dissociation and reinforces action-focused grounding with an Attention Consistency Reward within Group Relative Policy Optimization. We further construct FineActionR&R, combining temporally localized captions with hierarchical and temporal-causal reasoning data. Built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, FineActionVLM-R1 improves average MotionBench accuracy by 3.01 percentage points over its base model and achieves 91.50% on HAU-MCQ-Bench. Qualitative comparisons further indicate more faithful fine-grained action descriptions with fewer environment-induced hallucinations.

items.title_en: MonoLaDN: Language-Guided DeNoising for Monocular 3D Object Detection
items.abstract_en: Monocular 3D object detection offers a low-cost route to 3D perception, but it remains fundamentally ill-posed, since depth must be inferred from a single view. Recent transformer-based detectors learn geometry purely from image features and 3D box annotations, lacking the high-level semantic priors that vision-language models (VLMs) acquire from large-scale pretraining. VLMs offer such priors, but deploying one directly as a detector is impractical due to its heavy inference cost. We propose MonoLaDN, a language-guided denoising framework that transfers the geometric reasoning of a VLM into a monocular 3D detector while keeping the deployed model purely vision-based. During training, a frozen VLM produces structured reasoning about each object's occlusion, depth, dimension, and angle from the image and its ground-truth boxes. We encode this reasoning into queries, perturb them with noise, and train the detector to reconstruct the clean reasoning. Reconstructing the corrupted reasoning forces the detector's depth-guided features to internalize the VLM's geometric priors, so this knowledge remains available even after the reasoning path is discarded at inference, adding no latency or parameters to the deployed model. Experiments on KITTI 3D and nuScenes show that MonoLaDN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art detectors and generalizes well to new domains.

items.title_en: Quo Vadis, Driving Scene Reconstruction? Occlusion-Aware Gaussian Densification
items.abstract_en: While recent feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods enable efficient driving-scene reconstruction from surround-view images, their reliance on a single observation fundamentally hinders novel-view synthesis. Regions occluded in the input can become visible from novel viewpoints, leaving the reconstructed Gaussians under-constrained and incomplete. Moving beyond image-space inpainting for rendered views, we introduce OccSplat, a feed-forward framework whose core contribution is Occlusion-Aware Gaussian Densification, explicitly targeting missing scene geometry rather than missing pixels. By predicting new Gaussian primitives for unsupported regions, OccSplat completes the scene directly in the 3D representation. Specifically, OccSplat first identifies occluded regions that lack Gaussian support through Gaussian Occlusion Mapping. Gaussian Occlusion Completion then generates new primitives for these regions. The predicted primitives are integrated into the original representation to improve novel-view synthesis while retaining feed-forward inference without per-scene optimization. Experiments on the nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that OccSplat improves on the compared methods and yields particularly large gains in occluded regions, leading to more accurate and visually coherent driving-scene reconstruction.

items.title_en: Hijacking Cellular S-Acylation with Molecular Assemblies Rewires Oncogenic Signaling
items.title_zh: 劫持细胞 S-酰化：分子组装重塑致癌信号
items.abstract_en: KRAS-mutant cancers are generally treated by suppressing oncogenic signaling. Here, we investigated whether endogenous lipidation machinery could instead be used to spatially perturb that signaling. The thioester-bearing peptide precursor Stb-DPhe-DPhe-SAc (1) potently reduced PANC-1 cell viability and formed a palmitoylated product in treated cells. Synthetic palmitoylated 1 displayed increased assembly propensity, while fluorescent analogue 2 accumulated at the Golgi in a 2-bromopalmitate-sensitive manner. Compound 1 increased plasma-membrane-associated KRAS staining and ERK/AKT phosphorylation and induced pronounced LC3B and p62 remodeling. Inhibition of palmitoylation suppressed Golgi accumulation, attenuated the LC3B response, and rescued cell viability. These findings support a model in which cellular S-acylation drives organelle-localized molecular assembly that perturbs KRAS localization, oncogenic signaling, and associated stress responses. This work identifies endogenous lipidation machinery as a synthetic handle for spatial control of cancer signaling.
items.abstract_zh: KRAS 突变癌症通常通过抑制致癌信号来治疗。本文转而探究能否利用内源性脂化机器在空间上扰动该信号。携带硫酯的肽前体 Stb-DPhe-DPhe-SAc（1）可强效降低 PANC-1 细胞活力，并在处理细胞中形成棕榈酰化产物。合成的棕榈酰化 1 组装倾向增强，荧光类似物 2 以 2-溴棕榈酸酯敏感的方式在高尔基体富集。化合物 1 增加质膜相关 KRAS 染色及 ERK/AKT 磷酸化，并引起显著的 LC3B 与 p62 重塑。抑制棕榈酰化可阻断高尔基体富集、减弱 LC3B 响应并挽救细胞活力。这些结果支持如下模型：细胞 S-酰化驱动细胞器定位的分子组装，进而扰动 KRAS 定位、致癌信号及相关应激反应。该工作将内源脂化机器确立为空间控制癌症信号的合成操作点。
items.highlight_zh: 借细胞自身棕榈酰化在胞内组装，扰动 KRAS 致癌信号
items.digest_zh:
一、研究问题：KRAS 突变型癌症的常规思路是“把致癌信号压下去”。作者换了个角度：能不能反过来利用细胞自己的脂化修饰机器（S-酰化/棕榈酰化），在特定细胞器位置“搭”出超分子组装体，从空间上扰乱 KRAS 的信号传导？

二、方法：设计了一个带硫酯键的短肽前体 Stb-DPhe-DPhe-SAc（化合物 1），它可被细胞内的棕榈酰化机器修饰。作者合成了棕榈酰化版本的 1 来比较组装倾向，并制备荧光类似物 2 用于观察其在细胞内的定位；同时用棕榈酰化抑制剂 2-溴棕榈酸酯做阻断对照，验证机制依赖性。

三、结果：化合物 1 能强效降低胰腺癌 PANC-1 细胞的活力，并在细胞内生成棕榈酰化产物；棕榈酰化后组装倾向明显增强；荧光类似物 2 以 2-溴棕榈酸酯敏感的方式富集于高尔基体。化合物 1 还提高了质膜相关 KRAS 的染色信号以及 ERK/AKT 的磷酸化水平，并引起明显的 LC3B 与 p62 重塑（提示自噬/应激反应改变）。当棕榈酰化被抑制时，高尔基体富集消失、LC3B 响应减弱、细胞活力得到挽救——说明这些效应确实依赖内源脂化。

四、为何重要：工作提出一个机制模型：细胞 S-酰化驱动“细胞器定位的分子组装”，进而扰动 KRAS 定位、致癌信号与相关应激反应。它把内源脂化机器变成了一个可按空间精准操控癌症信号的合成“把手”，为 KRAS 突变肿瘤提供了不同于直接抑制信号的治疗思路。

items.title_en: Human lymphatic organoids reconstruct convergent developmental routes to functional lymphatic vessels
items.title_zh: 人淋巴管类器官重建通向功能性淋巴管的汇聚性发育路径
items.abstract_en: The lymphatic vasculature maintains fluid balance, regulates immune surveillance, and supports tissue repair, yet how human lymphatic vessels arise and acquire specialized functions remains poorly understood. Here, guided by single-cell and spatial analyses of human embryos, we found that both lateral plate and paraxial mesoderm converge on venous endothelial intermediates with cardinal vein-like characteristics prior to lymphatic specification. Informed by these developmental trajectories, we generated three-dimensional lymphatic organoids from human pluripotent stem cells through two distinct mesodermal routes. The organoids formed capillary-like vascular networks with emerging button-like junctions and distinct endothelial and stromal programs. The lymphatic organoids were transcriptionally benchmarked to human fetal lymphatic endothelium. The organoids supported immune-cell interactions and antigen accumulation and, following transplantation, exhibited interstitial tracer uptake and transport. These findings establish a platform for investigating how distinct developmental origins shape human lymphatic specification, vascular organization, and function, with applications to lymphatic disease modeling and tissue repair.
items.abstract_zh: 淋巴管系统维持体液平衡、调控免疫监视并支持组织修复，但人淋巴管如何发生并获特化功能仍不清楚。基于人胚胎单细胞与空间分析，本研究发现侧板中胚层与轴旁中胚层在淋巴特化前均先汇聚于具主静脉特征的静脉内皮中间态。据此，作者用人类多能干细胞经两条不同中胚层途径构建三维淋巴类器官：其形成毛细血管样网络与纽扣样连接，具独特的内皮与基质程序，转录组以人胎淋巴内皮为基准进行比对，可支持免疫细胞互作与抗原蓄积，移植后能摄取并转运间质示踪物。该平台可用于研究发育起源如何塑造人淋巴管特化、组织与功能，并服务于淋巴疾病建模与组织修复。
items.highlight_zh: 两条中胚层路径殊途同归，造出可移植的功能性人淋巴类器官
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：人体淋巴管在胚胎期如何形成、又如何获得专门功能，一直缺乏人源模型。
方法：作者先对人类胚胎做单细胞转录组与空间分析，追踪淋巴内皮的发育轨迹；再据此用人类多能干细胞，分别沿侧板中胚层和轴旁中胚层两条路径诱导三维淋巴类器官。
结果：两条路径都要先经过“主静脉样”的静脉内皮中间态再成为淋巴内皮，即发育上殊途同归。类器官能自组织成毛细血管样网络，出现淋巴管特有的纽扣样连接，并具独立的内皮与基质细胞程序；转录组与人胎淋巴内皮高度可比。功能上可与免疫细胞互作、蓄积抗原，移植入体内后还能摄取并转运组织间质中的示踪物。
意义：把“发育起源差异”变成可操作的人源实验平台，可用于研究不同起源如何塑造淋巴管形态与功能，也为淋巴水肿、淋巴管畸形等疾病建模和促淋巴管再生的组织修复提供工具。

items.title_en: Nematode species differ in susceptibility and response to the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys oligospora
items.title_zh: 不同线虫物种对捕食真菌少孢节丛孢的易感性与响应存在差异
items.abstract_en: Fungal predators of nematodes are widespread and represent promising candidates for biological control of parasitic nematodes. However, the behavioural and molecular mechanisms underlying nematode-fungus interactions remain poorly understood, especially for nematodes other than Caenorhabditis elegans. We investigated the interactions between the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys oligospora and three nematode species: (i) free-living C. elegans, (ii) fig-associated C. inopinata, and (iii) the free-living adult life cycle stage of the gastrointestinal parasite Strongyloides ratti. A. oligospora trapped S. ratti more efficiently than either C. elegans or C. inopinata. Behavioural analyses revealed species-specific differences in nematode locomotion. S. ratti moved slower, travelled shorter distances and showed lower displacement than Caenorhabditis spp. To test whether locomotion influences fungal trapping, we examined eight C. elegans mutants with hyper- or hypoactive locomotory phenotypes. Although both groups moved at similar speeds, hyperactive mutants showed greater displacement, which positively correlated with trap formation but did not explain trapping efficiency by A. oligospora. We investigated the fungal response during interaction with the three nematodes. Exposure to S. ratti, but not to Caenorhabditis spp, resulted in reduced sporulation and differential expression of sporulation-associated genes. In nematodes, myosin-related genes responded to A. oligospora in a species-specific manner, including upregulation in C. elegans and downregulation in S. ratti. These transcriptional changes may reflect alterations in muscle structure, including reduction in dense body and mitochondrial size in Caenorhabditis species but not S. ratti during A. oligospora exposure. Together, our findings demonstrate that both fungal and nematode responses are nematode species dependent. These results improve our understanding of nematode-fungus interactions and highlight the importance of nematode species when developing nematode-trapping fungi as a biological control agent.
items.abstract_zh: 食线虫真菌是寄生线虫生物防治的潜力手段，但相关互作机制研究多局限于秀丽隐杆线虫。本文比较捕食真菌少孢节丛孢（Arthrobotrys oligospora）与三种线虫的互作：自由生活的 C. elegans、与无花果相关的 C. inopinata，以及寄生线虫 Strongyloides ratti 的自由生活成虫期。A. oligospora 对 S. ratti 捕获效率最高，后者运动更慢、位移更小；8 个运动异常的 C. elegans 突变体显示位移与捕食器形成正相关，却不能解释捕获效率差异。接触 S. ratti 后真菌产孢减少、产孢相关基因差异表达，线虫肌球蛋白相关基因的响应也呈物种特异性。
items.highlight_zh: 捕食真菌对不同线虫捕获效率不同，互作具明显物种特异性
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：食线虫真菌是很有前景的线虫生物防治手段，但线虫与真菌之间的行为与分子互作在不同物种间为何不同，过去研究远少于模式线虫 C. elegans。
方法：以捕食真菌少孢节丛孢（A. oligospora）分别与三种线虫共培养——自由生活的 C. elegans、与无花果相关的 C. inopinata，以及胃肠道寄生线虫 Strongyloides ratti 的自由生活成虫期，结合运动行为定量与基因表达分析。
结果：真菌捕获 S. ratti 的效率最高；S. ratti 移动更慢、距离更短、位移更小。为检验运动是否决定捕获，作者测试 8 个运动亢进或迟钝的 C. elegans 突变体：亢进者位移更大，与捕食器形成正相关，却不能解释三种线虫被捕食效率的差异。真菌一侧，接触 S. ratti 后产孢减少、产孢相关基因差异表达，而接触两种 Caenorhabditis 无此变化。线虫一侧，肌球蛋白相关基因响应呈物种特异性（C. elegans 上调、S. ratti 下调），并可能对应肌肉结构改变。
意义：说明捕食真菌—线虫互作高度依赖物种，寄生线虫未必更难被捕获，为生物防治策略筛选提供线索。

items.title_en: Sexual interactions and local selection shape reproductive gene diversity and divergence
items.title_zh: 性相互作用与局部选择塑造生殖基因多样性与分化
items.abstract_en: Genes involved in genotype x genotype coevolution display unique patterns of nucleotide diversity and population divergence. In Drosophila melanogaster, Sex Peptide is a key sperm competition gene that is an outlier for both pi within populations and Fst between populations. This pattern is not predicted by current theoretical expectations of selective sweeps highlighting the need to develop predictions to identify genes experiencing balancing selection. We compared pi and FST in D. melanogaster populations to identify other genes following a co-evolutionary model that generates divergence and diversity. Multiple male and female genes that interact with Sex Peptide exhibited elevated FST x pi values. Genome-wide analyses also revealed an enrichment of genes critical for neuronal development, pointing to courtship evolution. Specifically, fruitless, its interacting genes, and a female behavior gene were identified as outliers. These parallel findings indicate that both sperm competition and mating behaviors are subject to co-evolutionary selection.

items.title_en: Mapping the regulatory wiring of endothelial cell differentiation reveals a critical role for Hippo mechanosignaling
items.title_zh: 绘制内皮细胞分化的调控连接图谱揭示Hippo机械信号传导的关键作用
items.abstract_en: At each step of development, stem cells encounter a branching decision to differentiate into one type of cell or another. This decision is executed through the action of competing gene programs that specify different cellular identities. Consequently, creating a comprehensive map of the gene programs that drive each branching step of human cell differentiation remains a long-sought goal of developmental and stem cell biology. Here, we introduce a framework combining genome-wide CRISPR screens, single-cell readouts, and gene program inference to systematically discover and characterize regulators of cell differentiation. This framework includes a method for CRISPR perturbations paired with single-cell RNA-seq called circular capture Perturb-seq (CC-Perturb-seq), which improves gRNA detection from split-pool combinatorial indexing protocols and enables perturbing many candidate regulators to map their effects on gene programs. We applied this framework to map how human pluripotent stem cells differentiate into arterial endothelial cells (ECs), and identified 174 regulators that promote or inhibit EC differentiation. By tracking gene programs across three stages of differentiation, we resolved when and how regulators divert cells toward alternative fates. This map revealed an unexpected requirement for the Hippo mechanosignaling pathway in EC specification. During lateral mesoderm differentiation, Hippo mechanosignaling was required to activate ETV2, the master transcriptional regulator of endothelial identity. Inhibiting Hippo blocked ETV2 even in the presence of VEGF and diverted progenitors to a mesenchymal fate in vitro. Likewise, Hippo signaling was required for maximal etv2 expression in developing zebrafish embryos. Conversely, pharmacologically activating the Hippo pathway increased the purity of both arterial and venous EC differentiation in vitro. Our framework thus identifies novel regulators of endothelial cell differentiation, improves stem-cell differentiation protocols via manipulation of mechanosignaling, and provides a generalizable platform for mapping the regulatory wiring of human development.

items.title_en: WheatPanRef: a unified linear pan-reference genome for wheat genomics
items.title_zh: WheatPanRef：用于小麦基因组学的统一线性泛参考基因组
items.abstract_en: Linear reference genomes provide coordinates for read mapping, variant discovery and multi-omics data integration, yet assembly-specific coordinate systems limit data reuse, particularly in the large, repetitive and polyploid wheat genome. Here, we present WheatPanRef, a scalable linear pan-reference and coordinate framework that integrates wheat sequence diversity within a stable coordinate system. We reconciled independent Chinese Spring assemblies by resolving structural and sequences discrepancies to constructed a 14.50-Gb consensus sequences CS-NP. Using CS-NP as backbone, we incorporated 4.37 Gb of non-redundant non-CS sequences from 37 diverse wheat accessions, generating WheatPanRef (18.87 Gb). WheatPanRef improves read-alignment performance and captures putative wild-relative introgressions and sequences absent or unanchored in conventional references. Bidirectional coordinate-translation system enables accurate projection between WheatPanRef and individual assemblies without remapping, facilitating genomic resource integration and reuse. WheatPanRef provides a common sequence and coordinate foundation for population-scale wheat genomics, with potential utility for genomic resource integration in other complex crops.

items.title_en: A hawkmoth's point of view - Innate symmetry preferences are informed by floral display and foraging function in an insect pollinator
items.title_zh: 天蛾的视角——昆虫传粉者的先天对称偏好受花卉展示与觅食功能影响
items.abstract_en: Floral visual cues are key for flower recognition and feeding in many pollinators. In insects, innate preferences for characteristic floral colour and pattern cues can guide naive foragers during their initial foraging. Symmetry is suggested to be one such foraging cue, since it is a remarkably conserved floral feature, with flowers mainly displaying radial or bilateral morphologies. Insect pollinators like honeybees, bumblebees, and hoverflies have been found to distinguish symmetry from asymmetry spontaneously or through learning. However, whether innate preferences for floral symmetry types, i.e. radial or bilateral, influence naive flower choice, and whether such preferences are linked to functional benefits during foraging remains uncertain.We investigated innate symmetry choice and its associated foraging function in the hummingbird hawkmoth (Macroglossum stellatarum). Besides relying on pattern cues for flower choice, these hawkmoths feed while hovering, making symmetry a valuable visual cue for flight and proboscis control. In choice assays, the hawkmoths' innate preferences for symmetry types depended on the floral display planes, with considerable differences between the horizontal and vertical displays. Tracking the hawkmoths during foraging revealed that in both display planes, the innately preferred patterns increased foraging success by guiding approach and nectary search. While an analysis of flowers visited by hawkmoths in nature did not reveal the same link between symmetry and display plane, a majority of plant species with vertically displayed flowers showed features matching those innately preferred by the hawkmoths. In this study, we provide the first instance of display-dependent innate foraging preferences and highlight how visuomotor strategies in nectivorous insects may have coevolved with flower features.

items.title_en: A Binuclear Cluster Supports Functional Asymmetry in Dark-Operative Protochlorophyllide Reductase
items.title_zh: 双核簇支撑暗操作型原叶绿素酸酯还原酶的功能不对称
items.abstract_en: Many photosynthetic bacteria rely on the nitrogenase-like dark-operative protochlorophyllide oxidoreductase (DPOR) to sustain (bacterio)chlorophyll synthesis in the dark. DPOR couples ATP hydrolysis to electron transfer from a reducing component (L-protein) to a catalytic component (NB-protein) that reduces protochlorophyllide. NB-protein is an 2{beta}2 heterotetramer, and each heterodimeric half contains an active site and a [Fe4S4] cluster. Although the two halves are identical, they react sequentially rather than in parallel. How the two halves communicate has remained unknown. Here we show, using Cu K-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy and cryo-EM, that the NB-protein tetramer interface holds a binuclear, sulfur-bridged [Cu2S2] cluster. Each Cu is reduced and three-coordinate, with short Cu-S and Cu-Cu distances (2.26 and 2.62 &Aring). Mutagenesis excludes the nearest cysteine as the bridging ligand, supporting inorganic sulfide as the most likely sulfur donor. To our knowledge, this is the first sulfide-bridged dicopper cluster identified in a protein. The cluster is conserved in three purple non-sulfur bacteria and connects the BchB C-terminal helices that contact opposing active sites. Loss of Cu abolishes DPOR activity and asymmetric L-protein binding without disturbing overall fold. We propose that the cluster relays substrate-binding information between active sites, suggesting a metal-mediated mechanism for cooperativity in nitrogenase-like enzymes.

items.title_en: Unlocking Targeted Underwater Delivery of Coral Probiotics
items.title_zh: 解锁珊瑚益生菌的靶向水下递送
items.abstract_en: The rapid global decline of coral reefs has intensified the need for innovative conservation strategies, including microbial therapies to enhance coral health and resilience. A major limitation, however, is the lack of effective delivery systems for administering Beneficial Microorganisms for Corals (BMCs). In this study, we present natural, biodegradable systems for the underwater delivery of probiotic bacteria to corals. Three customized alginate-based delivery formats (beads, hydrogels, and filaments) were developed and loaded with the probiotic Pseudoalteromonas peptidolytica. The materials were loaded with the bacterium at an average concentration of 10^(4) CFU/g of dry polymer and engineered to sink underwater while keeping their structural integrity over time. In vitro assays showed controlled release kinetics, with encapsulated probiotics remaining viable and capable of replication. In vivo experiments compared syringe-based inoculation with the application of alginate beads, hydrogels, and filaments to corals. Microbiome analyses performed before and after inoculation confirmed successful probiotic colonization following deployment of the alginate-based delivery systems. Relative abundance of the probiotic genus Pseudoalteromonas increased markedly in treated corals, reaching 11.5 % after 48 h with alginate beads, 12.7 % after 48 h with hydrogels, and 12.6 % after 24 h with filaments. Furthermore, the degradation mechanisms of the three delivery systems were investigated. As the first biomaterial-based underwater delivery systems specifically engineered for coral probiotics, these alginate-based materials provide a promising foundation for advancing microbial therapies in both controlled aquaria and natural reef environments.

items.title_en: MorphoProt: RNA-Conditioned Integration of Multiscale Histology for Spatial Protein Inference
items.title_zh: MorphoProt：RNA条件化的多尺度组织学整合用于空间蛋白质推断
items.abstract_en: Spatially resolved protein abundance reveals cellular states and tissue organization that RNA expression cannot fully capture, yet direct spatial protein profiling remains costly and limited in coverage. Histology images routinely accompany spatial transcriptomics and offer complementary morphological information for protein inference. Here, we introduce MorphoProt, a multimodal framework that jointly predicts spatial protein abundance from RNA expression, multiscale histology and tissue neighborhoods. MorphoProt uses RNA-guided cross-attention over five histological fields of view, so that the morphological context read for each spot is conditioned on its molecular state. The fused representation is refined by gated aggregation of RNA-derived information from physical and transcriptomic neighborhoods before joint protein prediction. On held-out sections of human tonsil, mouse spleen and human liver, MorphoProt achieves mean proteinwise Spearman correlations of 0.652, 0.604 and 0.372, outperforming matched RNA-only and graph-based baselines and the histology-based HIPI and multimodal SPRINT baselines in all three tissues. Combining fields of view, rather than any single one, carries the histology gain: in spleen and liver, the multiscale model outperforms every single-field model, and its learned scale preference separates white-pulp from red-pulp compartments. Predicted proteins preserve protein-defined tissue domains and their marker identity, and recover pathologist-annotated germinal centers as accurately as measured proteins.

items.title_en: FeatureMAP enables network-guided interpretation of untargeted metabolomics
items.title_zh: FeatureMAP 实现网络引导的非靶向代谢组学解读
items.abstract_en: Untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolomics generates thousands of features, but incomplete metabolite annotation and reliance on predefined pathways limit their biological interpretation. Here we present FeatureMAP, an LC-MS feature-centric computational framework that integrates multi-evidence metabolite annotation, network-guided refinement, metabolic module discovery, and structured large language model-based functional interpretation. Across ten public datasets, FeatureMAP improved MS1-based metabolite candidate prioritization while reducing annotation redundancy. In semi-synthetic benchmarks, FeatureMAP recovered coordinated metabolic perturbations, achieving 92% recovery of a simulated perturbation, and distinguished concurrent metabolic processes. Controlled benchmarks further evaluated functional interpretation under competing metabolite-level signals. Based on FeatureMAP, we additionally developed PhenoMAP, a phenotype-aware knowledge graph comprising 12,929 dysregulated metabolic modules from 501 human metabolomics studies spanning 326 phenotypes. Module-level comparisons revealed reproducible metabolic similarities across independent studies and biologically supported relationships among phenotypes. Application to Alzheimer's disease cerebrospinal fluid and cellular datasets identified convergent membrane-lipid alterations and implicated galactose-linked glycosphingolipid remodeling. Together, FeatureMAP and PhenoMAP enable network-grounded interpretation of incompletely annotated LC-MS metabolomics data and systematic investigation of metabolic dysregulation across biological conditions.
items.abstract_zh: 非靶向 LC-MS 代谢组学可产生数千个特征峰，但代谢物注释不完整、分析依赖预设通路，限制了生物学解读。本文提出 FeatureMAP——以 LC-MS 特征峰为中心的计算框架，整合多证据代谢物注释、网络引导的候选精简、代谢模块发现与基于结构化大语言模型的功能解读。在 10 个公开数据集中，FeatureMAP 改善了基于 MS1 的候选排序并减少注释冗余；半合成基准中可恢复协同代谢扰动，模拟扰动恢复率达 92%，并能区分并发的代谢过程。作者进一步构建 PhenoMAP 表型知识图谱，收录 501 项人类代谢组学研究的 12,929 个失调代谢模块，覆盖 326 种表型。应用于阿尔茨海默病脑脊液与细胞数据，发现一致的膜脂改变及半乳糖相关鞘糖脂重塑。
items.highlight_zh: 把注释不全的代谢组特征峰转为网络化、模块级的生物学解读
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：非靶向 LC-MS 代谢组学一次能测出成千上万个特征峰，但大量代谢物身份不明，分析又常依赖预设通路，导致生物学解释困难。
方法：作者提出 FeatureMAP，一个以特征峰为中心的计算框架，串联四步：整合多类证据的代谢物注释、用网络引导精简候选、发现代谢模块、以及基于结构化大语言模型的功能解读；并据此构建 PhenoMAP 表型知识图谱。
结果：在 10 个公开数据集上，FeatureMAP 改善了 MS1 层面的候选排序并减少注释冗余；半合成基准中能恢复协同的代谢扰动，模拟扰动恢复率达 92%，还能区分同时发生的多个代谢过程。PhenoMAP 汇集 501 项人类代谢组学研究、326 种表型、12,929 个失调代谢模块，模块层面比较显示独立研究之间存在可重复的代谢相似性。用于阿尔茨海默病脑脊液与细胞数据时，发现一致的膜脂改变，并指向半乳糖相关鞘糖脂重塑。
意义：让注释不完整的代谢组数据也能做网络化解读，并把零散研究整合为可系统查询的代谢失调图谱。

items.title_en: Earl Grey ParTEA: scalable, consistent transposable element annotation from pangenomes to deep phylogenetic scopes
items.title_zh: Earl Grey ParTEA：从泛基因组到深层系统发育范围的可扩展、一致转座元件注释
items.abstract_en: Transposable elements (TEs) are major drivers of genomic diversity, yet understanding their mobility and functional impact requires their accurate description in genomes. TE annotation is still typically performed genome-by-genome. TEs are often shared between some members of the same or closely related species. Hence, TE annotation with a library from a single reference misses families absent from that assembly, whereas building independent per-genome libraries fails to consistently surface shared TEs, hindering comparison. Here, we present Earl Grey ParTEA, a fully automated Snakemake pipeline extending the functionality of Earl Grey for comparative TE annotation across genome panels. ParTEA builds a single non-redundant TE library from all input genomes, resolves chimeric consensus sequences, and uses this shared library to annotate every genome, enabling direct comparison of TE family diversity, abundance, shared and private content, and activity landscapes. Optional modules provide TE library saturation analysis, BUSCO-based assembly quality control, and phylogenetic ordering of outputs. We applied ParTEA to sets of genomes spanning evolutionary scales: ten Arabidopsis thaliana accessions, ten Drosophila species, and ten species spanning the fungal kingdom. The Drosophila TE library expanded from 343 to 1,852 curated families including a previously missed rolling circle element with over 6,000 copies in D. miranda. The proportion of TE families shared across all genomes was highest within A. thaliana (97.3%), 37.7% across Drosophila species and only 0.5% across the set of fungi. ParTEA is available through Bioconda and represents a computationally efficient reproducible framework for comparative TE analysis in the era of large-scale genome analyses.

items.title_en: Harnessing catalytic knowledge to guide enzyme discovery and evolution with AlphaEnzyme
items.title_zh: 利用催化知识并结合AlphaEnzyme指导酶的发现与进化
items.abstract_en: Retrieving an enzyme for a target reaction provides a starting point for evolution, but predicting how to improve it remains difficult. This requires connecting evolutionary information with the structural and chemical context of catalysis. Here we present AlphaEnzyme, an enzyme foundation model built on a structure-grounded representation of an enzyme paired with its reaction, from which catalytic compatibility, kinetics and mutational response are read out together. On a time-separated benchmark, AlphaEnzyme achieves a top-1 catalyst retrieval success rate of 30.1%, against 17.2% for the strongest baseline. Michaelis constant predictions achieve the highest rank correlations among the compared methods, reaching 0.64 for enzymes sharing at most 40% identity with the kinetic training set. The model also enriches high-fitness TrpB variants at a budget of 16 candidates without target-specific fitness training. In prospective transaminase engineering, several prioritized variants exceed the parent, with the best design yielding a 30.4-fold increase in product signal in a lysate-based assay while retaining (R)-selectivity. Together, AlphaEnzyme provides a common molecular basis for selecting starting enzymes and prioritizing sequence changes for their improvement.

items.title_en: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction
items.title_zh: 一种用于结构域、功能位点和变异效应预测的蛋白质语言模型
items.abstract_en: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17,951 domain and 1,383 site classes. Across 2.3 million held-out proteins, PALM achieved domain- and site-occurrence F1 scores of 0.941 and 0.877, respectively, and retained substantial performance in proteins with <20% sequence identity to the training and validation data. PALM also substantially outperformed ESM3 annotation baseline. Without training on variant-pathogenicity labels, PALM embedding disruption distinguished 151,823 ClinVar missense variants more accurately than ESM2 embedding disruption (AUROC 0.835 versus 0.710), and combining PALM embedding disruption with the ESM2 likelihood-ratio signal reached an AUROC of 0.877. The same combined zero-shot score outperformed AlphaMissense on a benchmark dataset on 128,161 missense variants, that were derived from literature but not present in ClinVar database. At the protein level, PALM embeddings showed stronger CATH-Gene3D superfamily organization than frozen ESM2 and ESM3 embeddings, and improved prediction of experimental activation and repression effects when combined with ESM2. In a downstream case study, we demonstrated the ability to use PALM-derived embedding as proxy of deep mutational scanning (DMS), showcasing the broad application of PALM. Together, PALM converts curated residue-level knowledge into transferable and mechanistically interpretable representations that connect protein sequence, function, and variant consequence.

items.title_en: TIGRdisco: a tool for the discovery of TIGR arrays and TIGR-associated Tas proteins from nucleotide sequences
items.title_zh: TIGRdisco：一种从核苷酸序列中发现TIGR阵列和TIGR相关Tas蛋白的工具
items.abstract_en: Tandem Interspaced Guide RNA (TIGR)-TIGR-associated protein (Tas) systems mediate DNA targeting through a hypercompact Tas effector, guided by dual spacers within a tigRNA that is processed from TIGR arrays. TIGR-Tas loci are composed of a Tas coding sequence associated with TIGR arrays of short units in either dual-repeat or stem-loop architecture. Unlike CRISPR (Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) arrays that comprise units of direct repeats interspersed with unique spacers, units within the two distinct TIGR architectures only conform through extremely short box motifs, complicating detection. Here, we present TIGRdisco, an integrated tool capable of discovering both the Tas protein and its associated TIGR arrays directly from unannotated nucleotide sequences. TIGRdisco implements independent engines to detect the two array architectures through a motif-agnostic approach. We benchmarked TIGRdisco against a reference dataset of TIGR-Tas loci, recovering more than 80% of array units within its search window. Furthermore, TIGRdisco recovered arrays for loci within entire clades of Tas where associated arrays were unannotated in the reference. We found that these arrays largely contain non-canonical box motifs or unit lengths. Lastly, as a case study, we utilized TIGRdisco and successfully uncovered TIGR-Tas loci across metagenomic and genomic datasets.

items.title_en: Functional Assessment and Extended Culture of Human Pediatric Cardiac Tissue Slices for Preclinical Testing
items.title_zh: 用于临床前测试的人儿童心脏组织切片的功能评估与延长培养
items.abstract_en: Background: Living human myocardial slices preserve native tissue architecture, but their application to pediatric cardiac physiology or prolonged functional testing remains limited. We adapted a passive culture method for small surgical myocardial specimens obtained from patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Methods: Atrial and ventricular specimens were obtained from 41 cardiac surgery patients (7.7{+/-}11.1 years; 1 day-49 years). Myocardial tissue was sectioned into slices and studied acutely, or maintained under free floating, rocking cell culture conditions without electrical or mechanical stimulation. Calcium transients were recorded in response to external pacing (0.2-2 Hz) at baseline, and after isoproterenol or norepinephrine exposure. Selected preparations underwent viability, histological, and gene expression analyses. Results: Pacing evoked calcium transients were recorded from all four cardiac chambers, exhibiting expected frequency-dependent shortening. Mean interslice and intraslice coefficients of variation were 11.1% and 7.6%. Viability was 85.8 {+/-} 5.6% post-slicing and 78.8 {+/-} 5.0% after 3-5 hours. Calcium transients remained detectable through 178 days in atrial and 119 days in ventricular slices. Calcium transient durations were relatively stable during extended culture. Beta-adrenergic agonists shortened calcium transient durations (isoproterenol: 32% atrial, 25% ventricular at 0.3 Hz); responses to isoproterenol persisted to approximately 120 days in selected atrial slices and 60 days in ventricular slices. Selected histological features were preserved, although some extracellular matrix and apoptosis related transcripts changed. Conclusions: Small surgical specimens support repeated physiological measurements and pharmacological testing during extended passive culture, providing a platform for human developmental and disease-specific cardiac research.

items.title_en: Evaluating State-Transition Models in Short Resting-State fMRI with Continuous-Dynamics Controls
items.title_zh: 使用连续动力学对照评估短时静息态fMRI中的状态转移模型
items.abstract_en: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are widely used to describe changes in resting-state functional MRI as transitions between a finite set of inferred brain states. However, continuously varying brain activity can produce similar apparent transitions, raising questions about their biological validity. We tested whether discrete and continuous brain dynamics could be distinguished by predicting subsequent fMRI measurements, and if temporal filtering affects this distinction. We compared hidden Markov models (HMMs) with vector autoregressive (VAR) models, which predict signals from preceding measurements without assuming discrete states. Each time point contained signals from the seven Yeo functional networks. Both models used the same preceding observations to predict the next, with accuracy measured by the log probability density assigned to the observed signals. Across 864 simulated conditions, HMMs performed better in 139/144 unfiltered discrete-state cases, whereas VAR performed better in 67/72 continuous cases. Changing only the filter during testing increased the number of continuous cases favoring HMMs from 2/72 with fixed filtering to 68/72, despite unchanged underlying dynamics. We also analyzed resting-state fMRI from 270 ADNI participants (90 cognitively normal, 90 with mild cognitive impairment, and 90 with dementia). VAR outperformed HMM in 160/184 datasets with at least 180 time points and 60/86 shorter recordings. In simulations, HMMs inferred directional state transitions even from smoothly evolving activity without discrete switching. Thus, apparent fMRI state transitions do not necessarily indicate discrete underlying dynamics. Their interpretation requires comparison with continuous models and attention to temporal filtering.

items.title_en: Asymmetric detection of relative speed during motion-based figure-ground segregation
items.title_zh: 基于运动的图形-背景分离过程中相对速度的非对称检测
items.abstract_en: Visual motion can support figure-ground segregation when a local region moves at a different speed from its background, but whether faster- and slower-than-background targets are detected equally well, and how any asymmetry depends on background speed and motion reliability remains incompletely understood. We measured relative-speed detection thresholds in four human observers using an eight-alternative forced-choice localization task. On each trial, one of eight random-dot patches at 10-degree eccentricity moved either faster or slower than a surrounding moving background. Relative-speed detection thresholds were measured with adaptive staircases at five background speeds (2.5-30 deg/s) under 100% and 60% motion coherence. In every observer, slower targets required larger relative-speed differences for detection than faster targets. This increment-decrement asymmetry was strongest at low background speeds and diminished as speed increased. Reducing motion coherence elevated thresholds overall but disproportionately impaired detection of slower targets, amplifying the asymmetry, most strongly at the lowest measurable speeds. Under 100% coherence, increment detection showed approximately Weber-like scaling from 10 to 30 deg/s, whereas under reduced coherence both increment and decrement Weber fractions decreased with increasing background speed. Relative-speed detection therefore depends on the sign of the speed difference, background speed, and motion reliability. The faster-target advantage is consistent with faster-speed weighting reported in cortical area MT and with natural-scene statistics showing that figural regions tend to move faster than their backgrounds, suggesting that relative-speed sensitivity may contribute to motion-based figure-ground segregation. More broadly, such increment-decrement asymmetries can reveal biases in how sensory signals are represented and read out.

items.title_en: Dynamic allocation of MurJ coordinates bacterial growth and division
items.title_zh: MurJ的动态分配协调细菌生长与分裂
items.abstract_en: Rod-shaped bacteria grow by inserting peptidoglycan into the lateral cell wall during elongation and into the septal cell wall during division. These two modes of growth are driven by distinct peptidoglycan synthesis machineries that consume the shared precursor Lipid II and must be coordinated so that cell enlargement remains matched to division. However, how cells spatially allocate this shared precursor, and whether Lipid II translocation itself contributes to this coordi-nation, remain unclear. Here we show that the spatial distribution of the essential Lipid II flippase MurJ coordinates this balance in Escherichia coli. Increasing nonseptal MurJ abundance shifted cell-wall synthesis toward elongation and reduced septal synthesis. Single-molecule tracking revealed that MurJ diffuses throughout the membrane but is transiently captured at the division site, rather than stably incorporated into the septal synthesis machinery. This recruitment requires active septal cell-wall synthesis, but not ongoing Lipid II synthesis or flipping, indicating that MurJ recruitment is coupled to the active synthesis machinery rather than to substrate availability or transport. Thus, activation of septal synthesis creates transient MurJ capture at the division site, providing a mechanism to preferentially supply Lipid II for septal growth during cytokinesis. These findings reveal a capture-and-release mechanism that dynamically enriches MurJ at active division sites and thereby coordinates elongation and division in bacterial cells.

items.title_en: T cell transcriptomes in simulated microgravity in vivo
items.abstract_en: Spaceflight exposes astronauts to a combination of stressors, among which microgravity remains the least well characterized at the level of human immune cell function. We examined the in vivo effect of long-term simulated microgravity (SMG) on T cell transcriptomes in ten healthy male volunteers who completed a three-week dry immersion protocol without countermeasures. Peripheral blood was collected at five time points covering a pre-immersion baseline (day -7), three intra-exposure time points (days 7, 14 and 21) and a recovery time point one week after the end of exposure (day 28). CD3+ T cells were isolated and analysed by RNA-seq, with differential expression assessed per volunteer and KEGG pathway enrichment used to identify the most affected gene networks. SMG was associated with transcript-level changes in genes mapping to key molecular pathways, including those involved in cell proliferation, cell-cycle regulation, maintenance of genome integrity, and oncogenic and tumour-suppressor networks. Hub genes shared across the most significant pathways were differentially expressed in the majority of volunteers. A notable finding was pronounced inter-individual heterogeneity: samples clustered primarily by volunteer identity, yet a coordinated temporal shift during exposure and a partial return toward baseline by day 28 were detectable across donors, and these changes occurred in the absence of detectable systemic inflammation. These results indicate that SMG is associated with altered T cell transcriptional programs in vivo and that the response is sufficiently variable between individuals to favor personalized rather than uniform countermeasure strategies.

items.title_en: Genome evolution and glycosyltransferase diversification shape asperosaponin biosynthesis in Dipsacus asperoides
items.abstract_en: Deciphering the genomic and enzymatic features associated with high-abundance specialized metabolism is important for understanding and engineering bioactive natural product biosynthesis. Asperosaponin , a hederagenin-based saponin, accumulates at exceptionally high levels in Dipsacus asperoides roots and is by far the predominant triterpenoid saponin. Here, by integrating a chromosome-level genome assembly with comparative genomics, transcriptomics, metabolite profiling, and biochemical characterization, we reconstructed a major biosynthetic route to asperosaponin and identified diversification of triterpenoid-associated gene families. Functional analyses revealed an ordered glycosylation sequence in which DaUGT73GZ2 preferentially accepts C-3-glycosylated substrates retaining a free C-28 carboxyl group, thereby establishing a C-3-before-C-28 glycosylation order during asperosaponin biosynthesis. Phylogenetic and biochemical analyses further uncovered functional differentiation among UGT85CA enzymes involved in C-3 arabinosylation, while genomic and expression analyses revealed lineage-specific patterns of pathway gene duplication and transcriptional regulation. Together, these findings identify genomic, enzymatic, and transcriptional features associated with the distinctive, high-abundance triterpenoid saponin profile of D. asperoides roots and provide a framework for understanding and engineering triterpenoid saponin biosynthesis.

items.title_en: Salinity adaptation in date palm (Phoenix dactylifera): evidence for selective sweeps at Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) genes
items.abstract_en: The date palm is a high salinity tolerant fruit tree grown mainly in the region spanning from North Africa to parts of South Asia. Climate change models of this region indicate the possibility of increasing salinity in the future. The Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) pathway is crucial for salinity tolerance in plants, serving as a primary defense mechanism by facilitating sodium exclusion. To better understand date palms' salt tolerance, we analyzed variation in SOS pathway genes in a set of 197 date palm genomes collected from across the range of cultivation. Here, we show evidence for selective sweeps in multiple SOS pathway genes. A single major pdSOS1 haplotype is at very high frequency in Eastern and Western subpopulations, with a minor, likely ancestral haplotype still present in both geographical locations. Allele-specific gene expression analysis showed differences in salt-treated roots between swept and ancestral haplotypes. Interestingly, sequence-based analysis of the pdSOS1 haplotype suggested a second, much earlier introgression event between P. theophrasti and date palm, though direction is unclear. This event happened before both the selective sweep and the previously reported recent introgression to date palm. We identified a MITE transposable element inserted into a pdSOS1 intron on the swept haplotype, and a similar insertion was found in an intron of the SOS2 paralog pdCIPK8. Both insertions are unique to date palm among Phoenix species. The pdCIPK8 haplotype containing the MITE is also at high frequency in both populations. Further analysis showed evidence for a selective sweep spanning the pdSOS3 region in the western population that shares similarity to an Eastern haplotype spanning the promoter region only. Slower extended haplotype homozygosity decay surrounding the genes in the western population suggests that the swept haplotype originated in the East and spread to the West in all cases. Altogether, our data provide evidence of selective sweeps in the date palm SOS pathway and may go to explaining how this species has developed such high salinity tolerance.

items.title_en: TRPP Ion Channels Function in the π-Conformation Rather Than the α-Conformation
items.abstract_en: PKD2 (TRPP1) is a TRPP ion channel whose dysfunction causes autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Understanding its conformational states and gating mechanism is important for elucidating its function and for structure-based drug discovery. Cryo-EM structures of WT-PKD2 contain a local {pi}-helical turn in the S6 pore-lining helix ({pi}-conformation). In contrast, a fully -helical S6 (-conformation) was observed in the gain-of-function mutant F604P-PKD2 and interpreted as the open state, leading to the proposed {pi}-to- activation mechanism. However, whether the -conformation can support function has never been directly established. Here, using molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate the functional properties of the -and {pi}-conformations of PKD2. The -conformation remains dewetted unless the lower gate is widened beyond the conformational range observed in mammalian TRP channels. By contrast, the {pi}-conformation supports pore hydration and ion conduction following a small opening of the L677 gate, with simulated conductance comparable to experimental measurements. The closely related PKD2L1 (TRPP2) channel shows a similar dependence on conformation, with a hydrated {pi}-conformation and a dewetted -conformation. Together, these findings challenge the assignment of the -conformation as the conductive state and support a model in which the {pi}-conformation represents the functionally relevant state of TRPP channels. This model suggests that activation may involve an -to-{pi} transition rather than the previously proposed {pi}-to- transition, providing a new framework for understanding TRPP channel gating. This work sheds light on the molecular basis of polycystin channel dysfunction and could facilitate the development of PKD2-targeted therapeutic strategies for ADPKD.

items.title_en: HiSpoT: a novel one-tube dual-barcode PCR method for NGS spoligotyping amplicon library preparation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex
items.abstract_en: Tuberculosis remains one of the leading infectious causes of death globally, making rapid, accurate, and affordable strain typing essential for effective outbreak tracking and epidemiological surveillance. To address the limitations and high costs of current typing methods, we developed a novel one-tube, dual-barcode PCR method for preparing targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) amplicon libraries for spoligotyping of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC), which we termed HiSpoT (High-throughput Spoligotyping by Targeted next generation sequencing). The assay targets 43 conserved spacer oligonucleotides in the CRISPR direct repeat (DR) region and is presented here together with the previously unpublished, difficult-to-design dual-barcode primer set needed to multiplex 96 samples in a single tube. HiSpoT is accurate, fast, high-throughput, and low-cost, eliminating the need for a commercial NGS library preparation kit. Because HiSpoT is PCR-based, the resulting spoligotypes remain directly comparable with the large PCR-based spoligotype databases accumulated over decades, enabling rapid outbreak tracking and biogeographic characterization of the tuberculosis burden of a country, while higher-resolution whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data are obtained. Analysis of 288 clinical MTBC isolates from Israel (2020-2022) demonstrated a broad range of genetic lineages, and comparison of 79 isolates analyzed by both HiSpoT and WGS showed 70% full concordance, with essentially all discrepancies attributable to single-spacer insertion-element disruptions of PCR primer sites. We also present two open-source Google Colab Python tools, Spoligotyping_MTBC_gcl and its condensed HiSpoT_Spoligotyping_v8_ready VIBE variant, freely available on GitHub, which automatically process Illumina paired-end fastq output from HiSpoT or WGS and report binary and octal spoligotypes, spoligo international types (SIT), and MTBC family assignments with accompanying quality-control reports.

items.title_en: Dendrite Control Theory: A Unifying Framework Bridging Neuronal Morphology And Dendritic Voltage Behavior
items.abstract_en: Control theory and dendritic computation have revolutionized their respective fields, yet they rarely converge. Here, we use control theory as a framework to reveal how dendritic morphology and synaptic input organization constrain structural resilience and energy cost. Treating diverse dendritic trees as connected network nodes, we demonstrate that the degree of structural symmetry dictates easy- versus hard-to-access control states. Notably, control inputs restricted solely to peripheral terminal branches are mathematically sufficient to govern the voltage states of the entire dendrite and soma, granting striking resilience against input loss elsewhere. Conversely, limiting input dimensionality amplifies voltage fluctuations and metabolic costs. These findings expose fundamental biophysical trade-offs between wiring cost, functional flexibility, robustness, and energy efficiency, suggesting interneurons generally exhibit higher resilience while excitatory neurons feature superior controllability. We introduce 'Dendrite Control Theory' as a rigorous engineering framework linking neuronal morphology directly to computation and robustness, offering a new neuroscience research paradigm.

items.title_en: Genome-wide chromatin accessibility during early embryogenesis in a generalist cichlid fish
items.abstract_en: Background Lake Malawi's haplochromine cichlids are one of the most rapid and species-rich vertebrate adaptive radiations known, generating hundreds of species within < 1 million years, yet how regulatory regions shape their embryonic development remains poorly understood. Astatotilapia calliptera, a generalist riverine lineage and proxy for the ancestral stock that seeded this radiation, offers a developmental chromatin baseline against which regulatory divergence in specialised lineages can be compared. Results We generated genome-wide ATAC-seq profiles of A. calliptera embryos across three developmental stages (3, 7 and 12 days post-fertilisation, dpf), identifying 550,876-701,889 accessible chromatin peaks per stage. Accessible chromatin was enriched at gene promoters and at both highly conserved and accelerated conserved noncoding elements at every stage. The functional repertoire of accessible-promoter genes shifted across development, from early patterning at 3 dpf to the broadest regulatory repertoire at 7 dpf, and an increasingly neural- and locomotory-behaviour-enriched repertoire by 12 dpf, coinciding with post-hatching motor maturation. Differential accessibility showed that chromatin opening, rather than closing, dominates the earliest transitions (3 vs 7 and 3 vs 12 dpf), driven mostly by general metabolic genes, whereas the smaller, later 7 vs 12 dpf transition combined targeted gains at tissue-remodelling and apoptosis genes with losses at genes governing early neural and retinal patterning; almost all of these losses (96%) were at promoters that had opened between 3 and 7 dpf, indicating transient rather than sustained opening. Transcription factor (TF) footprinting identified stage-specific regulatory activity among developmentally important TFs, while the broader TF-promoter network remained topologically stable across all three stages, built around conserved hub regulators of core neural and sensory patterning genes e.g., SOX2, FOXG1, PTF1A, SOX10. This suggests that wiring is established early and largely maintained, following the hourglass model, with developmental progression driven by changes in activity of this conserved programme. Conclusions Together, these findings establish the first embryonic epigenomic resource for A. calliptera, revealing a developmental chromatin landscape of broad early opening and progressive functional specialisation, and providing a comparative framework for understanding how regulatory evolution has shaped Lake Malawi cichlid diversification.

items.title_en: Prokaryotic homologs of the major vault protein form engineerable vault nanocapsules
items.abstract_en: Vaults are the largest ribonucleoprotein particles in eukaryotic cells, built from 78 copies of the major vault protein (MVP), yet their function remains unknown four decades after their discovery. MVP homologs occur in prokaryotes and bacteriophages, but whether they form vaults is unknown. Here, we show that prokaryotic and bacteriophage MVP homologs assemble into vault particles. We surveyed approximately 15 billion proteins, found MVP homologs in 29 bacterial and 4 archaeal phyla, and used size-exclusion chromatography to rapidly screen and isolate vault particles of eight homologs expressed in Escherichia coli. Cryo-electron microscopy structures of the phage homolog L05 at high resolution reveal a shell of 96 MVP chains enclosing a volume ~25% larger than human vaults, among the largest protein shells of defined size outside virus capsids. Prokaryotic MVPs typically carry seven wall repeats and eukaryotic MVPs nine, and adding wall repeats to L05 yields larger vaults. Prokaryotic vaults expand the known diversity of vault architecture and offer a tractable system for studying vault assembly and a size-tunable scaffold for cargo encapsulation.

items.title_en: Combined Use of Topic-Analysis and LLMs on Online Peer-to-Peer Medicaid Discussions to Detect the Impact of HR1 on Individuals' Medicaid Experience Across The US
items.abstract_en: Medicaid is a government program providing benefits to 1 in 5 people in the US, including medical care for children and adults, long-term care for the elderly, and home/community-based services for the disabled[1]. Effective January 1st 2027, HR1 (One Big Beautiful Bill) passed by Congress will implement new administrative requirements to Medicaid expected to strip benefits from 1.8 million adults, children, and seniors[2]. As each US state administers Medicaid independently, the timing, frequency, and severity of those losses may vary across states. Monitoring that human impact requires an detailed ongoing view of affected individuals and their families. To monitor the human-impact of HR1, this work develops a proof-of-concept using topic analysis and LLMs to generate detailed categorization of individuals' Medicaid experiences across multiple states and over time.

items.title_en: Prospective In-silico Simulation of the VESALIUS-CV Trial Using Biomedical Knowledge Graph and Real-World Data-Driven AI Modeling
items.abstract_en: Cardiovascular outcomes trials are lengthy and costly. In silico trial simulation using real-world data may support earlier decision-making, but evidence generated before trial results are disclosed remains limited. We applied a semi-mechanistic machine learning framework integrating patient-level real-world data with knowledge graph-derived drug representations to simulate the VESALIUS-CV trial of evolocumab versus placebo before its results were public, using a locked model and prespecified trial design aligned with the trial protocol. Patient-level time-to-event predictions were aggregated into virtual trial arms to estimate cumulative incidence, hazard ratios (HR), confidence intervals (CI), and p-values for three-point major adverse cardiovascular events. In retrospective evaluation of the model's patient-level predictive performance, time-dependent areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.80 to 0.90 across follow-up horizons. In evaluation of retrospective trial-level predictive performance across 22 cardiovascular trials, the model predicted trial meeting the primary outcome with an accuracy of 0.91 (95% CI 0.77-1) and F1 score of 0.95 (95%CI 0.86-1). The prospective simulation predicted a significant reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events with evolocumab (HR 0.78; 95%CI, 0.70 to 0.87) at 54 months. The trial subsequently reported a HR of 0.75 (95% confidence interval, 0.65 to 0.86) at a median follow-up of 55 months, with progressive separation of event curves in both the simulation and the trial. The prospective simulation was concordant with the direction, magnitude, and temporal dynamics of the observed treatment effect, supporting in silico simulation as a tool for early decision-making, trial design, and de-risking in cardiovascular drug development.

items.title_en: Synthetic epigenomes for open cross-platform episignature classifiers
items.abstract_en: DNA methylation (DNAm) signature (episignature) classifiers support diagnosis of rare diseases. Yet episignature testing is confined to a dedicated array platform, and most classifiers are neither openly available nor fully reproducible. Laboratories cannot train their own classifiers as positive controls are scarce and cannot be shared under privacy regulations. Here, we develop and release MethaDory, a framework to train episignature classifiers using synthetic DNAm profiles generated in silico from control data and summary statistics of affected individuals from any platform of interest. We trained 188 classifiers spanning 102 rare disorders and validated 154 across 915 individuals with an episignature-associated diagnosis, 533 healthy controls profiled with DNAm arrays, Oxford Nanopore, and PacBio sequencing, together with 7 international centres. MethaDory achieved an average F1 0.9 on arrays, matching or outperforming existing approaches. We show MethaDory classifier application to long-read genome data, facilitating diagnoses in unsolved cases and in ultra-rapid diagnostic settings.

items.title_en: ECG-Derived Synthetic Left Ventricular Mechanics Predict Mortality After Acute Myocardial Infarction and Fatal Myocardial Infarction in the General Population
items.abstract_en: Background: Left ventricular (LV) mechanical function predicts outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Recovering these parameters from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) could enable point-of-care risk assessment wherever an ECG is acquired. Objectives: To determine whether ECG-derived synthetic LV mechanics predict all-cause mortality after AMI and myocardial infarction (MI)-specific mortality in the general population and add information beyond the GRACE score and ejection fraction. Methods: Synthetic peak systolic (s') and early diastolic (e') mitral annular velocities and mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) were derived from the 12-lead ECG by a previously validated generative adversarial network, applied without retraining and blinded to outcome. Associations were assessed in an AMI cohort (n=1,065) by Cox regression and a population cohort (n=219,564) by Fine-Gray models. Incremental value was tested against GRACE, three AI-ECG reduced ejection fraction (EF) models, and measured LVEF. Results: In the AMI cohort (109 deaths; median follow-up 1.44 years), all three parameters predicted all-cause mortality (each P<0.001). Synthetic e' was the sole independent predictor after adjustment for clinical covariates (HR=0.90 per 1 cm/s; 95% CI 0.84-0.98) and for GRACE (HR=0.90; 0.83-0.97; P=0.006). In the post-discharge cohort (n=1,017; 61 deaths), synthetic e' improved discrimination beyond GRACE (C-index 0.67 to 0.70; HR=0.84 per 1 cm/s; 95% CI 0.76-0.93; P=0.001) and remained independent of AI-ECG-predicted and measured LVEF (HR 0.84-0.86 per 1 cm/s; all P[≤]0.004), contributing 28-46% of each model's prognostic information. In the population cohort (817 MI deaths; median follow-up 3.42 years), all three predicted MI-specific mortality after adjustment for age, sex, and ECG abnormalities, MAPSE showing the largest effect (sHR=0.49; 95% CI 0.37-0.65), with s' (sHR=0.78; 0.72-0.84) and e' (sHR=0.87; 0.82-0.93) also predictive (each P<0.001). Conclusions: ECG-derived synthetic LV mechanical parameters predict all-cause mortality after AMI and fatal MI in the general population, adding information beyond the GRACE score and LVEF. Keywords: electrocardiogram; tissue Doppler imaging; generative adversarial network; myocardial infarction; mortality prediction; risk stratification.

items.title_en: Learning Time-Varying Connectomes for Stable Behavior Across Development
items.title_zh: 学习时变连接组以在发育过程中实现稳定行为
items.abstract_en: Neural circuits must maintain functionality to drive effective behavior while their size, topology, geometry, and intrinsic dynamics change across development. To model developing visuomotor circuits and behavior, we investigated whether a single compact generative encoding could produce functional recurrent controllers across such changes.
